info.name: Avalara AvaTax (TCH Sandbox)
info.description:
# Avalara AvaTax: TCH Integration

Complete Postman collection covering all Avalara AvaTax REST API v2 endpoints required for the TCH (The Clearing House) tax integration with Salesforce/Fonteva.

## What this collection covers

| Folder | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| 1\. Authentication | Verify API connectivity and credentials are valid |
| 2\. Address Validation | Normalize and validate US/CA addresses before tax calculation |
| 3\. Tax Calculation | Calculate sales tax in real time (estimates and final invoices) |
| 4\. Tax Lifecycle | Full transaction lifecycle: create → commit → void |
| 5\. ECM | Manage tax exemption certificates and CertExpress invitations |
| 6\. Definitions & Lookup | Reference data: tax codes, entity use codes, nexus config |

## Setup

1. Go to the collection **Variables** tab
    
2. Set `accountId` — your Avalara Account ID
    
3. Set `licenseKey` — generated at Avalara admin portal: Settings → Reset License Key
    
4. Set `companyCode` — TCH company code in Avalara
    
5. Set `environment` — `sandbox` or `production`
    
6. Run folders in order: **1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5 → 6**
    

## Authentication

All requests use **Basic Auth** (inherited from the collection) with `accountId` as username and `licenseKey` as password. Avalara does not use OAuth 2.0 for AvaTax REST v2.

## References

- Authentication Guide: [https://developer.avalara.com/avatax/authentication-in-rest/](https://developer.avalara.com/avatax/authentication-in-rest/)
    
- AvaTax API Reference: [https://developer.avalara.com/products/avatax/api/](https://developer.avalara.com/products/avatax/api/)
    
- ECM API Reference: [https://developer.avalara.com/products/ecm/api/certcapture/](https://developer.avalara.com/products/ecm/api/certcapture/)
    
- Developer Guide (Transactions): [https://developer.avalara.com/avatax/dev-guide/transactions/](https://developer.avalara.com/avatax/dev-guide/transactions/)
    
- Developer Guide (Exemptions): [https://developer.avalara.com/avatax/dev-guide/exemptions/](https://developer.avalara.com/avatax/dev-guide/exemptions/)

item.name: 1. Authentication

request.description:
## Ping — Test Connectivity & Authentication

**API Method:** `Ping`
**Purpose:** Diagnoses connectivity between your application and the Avalara API. Returns authentication status, API version, and account details.

**Why we need it:** This is the first request to run — it confirms the License Key is valid and the sandbox/production URL is reachable. If this fails, nothing else will work.

**Expected response:**
- `authenticated: true` → credentials are valid
- `authenticatedUserName` → the account identity
- `version` → current AvaTax API version

**Doc:** https://developer.avalara.com/products/avatax/api/methods/Utilities/Ping/

## Ping — Unauthenticated (Negative Test)

**API Method:** `Ping`
**Purpose:** Sends the same Ping request but with no credentials. Confirms that the API properly rejects unauthenticated access.

**Why we need it:** Ensures that `authenticated: true` in request 1.1 is genuinely validating credentials, not just returning true for all requests.

**Expected response:**
- `authenticated: false`
- Status 200 (Ping always returns 200, auth status is in the body)

## QueryCompanies — Get Company ID

**API Method:** `QueryCompanies`
**Purpose:** Lists all companies configured in this Avalara account. Retrieves the numeric `companyId` and `companyCode`.

**Why we need it:** The ECM endpoints (folder 5) require the numeric `companyId` in the URL path, while tax calculation endpoints use the string `companyCode`. This request auto-saves both.

**What it returns:**
- Company name, code, ID
- Company configuration details
- Tax profile information

**Auto-sets variable:** `companyId` (from the first company returned)

**Doc:** https://developer.avalara.com/products/avatax/api/methods/Companies/QueryCompanies/

item.description:
## Purpose

Verify that the Avalara API is reachable and that the provided credentials (Account ID + License Key) are valid. This must pass before any other request in the collection will work.

## How it works

Avalara uses HTTP Basic Authentication. The `accountId` and `licenseKey` are combined as `accountId:licenseKey`, Base64-encoded, and sent in the `Authorization: Basic {encoded}` header. This is handled automatically by Postman via the collection-level auth settings.

## Requests

- **1.1 Ping (With Auth)** — confirms credentials are accepted (`authenticated: true`)
- **1.2 Ping (Without Auth)** — confirms the API correctly rejects unauthenticated requests
- **1.3 GetCompanies** — retrieves the company list and auto-saves the numeric `companyId` (needed by ECM endpoints in folder 5)

## Doc
https://developer.avalara.com/avatax/authentication-in-rest/

## ResolveAddress — Valid Address

**API Method:** `ResolveAddress` (POST)
**Purpose:** Validates a US/Canadian address against Avalara's address database. Returns the normalized (corrected) address and geolocation coordinates.

**Test scenario:** Sends the White House address — a known valid address that should resolve cleanly.

**Expected response:**
- `validatedAddresses[]` with corrected street, city, state, zip
- `latitude` / `longitude` coordinates
- `resolutionQuality` indicating match precision

**Minimum required fields:** `postalCode` alone, OR `line1 + city + region`, OR `line1 + postalCode`

**Doc:** https://developer.avalara.com/products/avatax/api/methods/Addresses/ResolveAddress/

  "city": "Nowheresville",

  "country": "US"
}

request.description:
## ResolveAddress — Invalid Address (Negative Test)

**API Method:** `ResolveAddress` (POST)
**Purpose:** Tests how the API responds to an invalid/non-existent address. Verifies that the Apex error handling logic will receive meaningful error messages.

**Test scenario:** Sends a fake address with invalid state code (ZZ) and zip (00000).

**Expected response:**
- `messages[]` array with validation warnings/errors
- Or HTTP 400 with error details

**Why we need it:** The Apex `AvalaraAddressService` must handle invalid addresses gracefully and surface clear errors to the user.

item.description:
## Purpose

Validate and normalize US and Canadian addresses using Avalara's address resolution engine. Returns the corrected address, geolocation coordinates (latitude/longitude), and a quality indicator.

## Why it matters for TCH

Sales tax is jurisdiction-based — the tax rate depends on the exact location of the buyer (state, county, city, district). An incorrect or incomplete address can map to the wrong jurisdiction, resulting in incorrect tax calculation. Address validation ensures the `shipTo` address sent to `CreateTransaction` is accurate.

## When to use in the integration

- **Option A:** Validate on every checkout (adds ~100ms per API call but guarantees accuracy)
- **Option B:** Validate once when the address is saved on the Account/Contact record (recommended — avoids repeated callouts)

## Requests

- **2.1 Valid Address** — tests with a known good address (White House)
- **2.2 Invalid Address** — tests error handling with a fake address

## Doc
https://developer.avalara.com/products/avatax/api/methods/Addresses/ResolveAddress/

item.name: 3. Tax Calculation

request.description:
## CreateTransaction — SalesOrder (Estimate)

**API Method:** `CreateTransaction`
**Purpose:** Creates a temporary tax estimate. SalesOrder transactions are NOT saved in Avalara — they are disposable calculations meant for cart/checkout preview.

**When TCH will use this:** Every time a customer views their cart or enters the checkout page, this call shows the estimated tax before payment.

**Key fields:**
- `type: SalesOrder` — temporary, not recorded
- `companyCode` — TCH company in Avalara
- `customerCode` — Salesforce Account or Contact ID
- `addresses.shipFrom` — TCH business address (origin)
- `addresses.shipTo` — customer address (destination/jurisdiction)
- `lines[].taxCode` — Avalara tax category for the product

**Expected response:**
- `totalTax` — total tax for the transaction
- `lines[].tax` — tax per line item
- `status` — should be `Temporary`

**Doc:** https://developer.avalara.com/products/avatax/api/methods/Transactions/CreateTransaction/

exec: pm.test('NT line has zero tax', function () {

request.description:
## CreateTransaction — SalesOrder (Multiple Lines & Tax Codes)

**API Method:** `CreateTransaction`
**Purpose:** Tests how Avalara handles multiple line items with different tax codes in a single transaction. This simulates a real Fonteva cart with mixed product types.

**Test scenario — 3 lines with different tax treatments:**
- Line 1: `P0000000` (Tangible Personal Property) — standard taxable goods
- Line 2: `SW054000` (SaaS/Software Subscription) — taxable in some states, exempt in others
- Line 3: `NT` (Non-Taxable) — should always return $0 tax

**Why we need it:** TCH sells different product types (memberships, software, donations). Each type maps to a different Avalara Tax Code and is taxed differently depending on the state. This request confirms the tax engine handles mixed carts correctly.

**Expected response:**
- Lines 1 and 2 should have non-zero tax (if nexus is configured for NY)
- Line 3 (NT) should have exactly $0 tax
- `totalTax` should be the sum of all line-level taxes

## CreateTransaction — SalesOrder (Exempt Customer)

**API Method:** `CreateTransaction`
**Purpose:** Tests the tax exemption mechanism. When a customer has a valid exemption (via `customerUsageType` or an ECM certificate), Avalara should return $0 tax.

**Test scenario:** Same product and addresses as 3.1, but the customer is marked as `customerUsageType: A` (Federal Government — exempt from sales tax in most states).

**How exemptions work in the integration:**
1. **Via Entity Use Code** — set `customerUsageType` in the request (e.g., `A` = Federal Gov, `B` = State Gov, `E` = Charitable/Religious). Used here.
2. **Via ECM Certificate** — if the customer has a valid certificate in Avalara's ECM, the exemption is applied automatically when the correct `customerCode` is sent.
3. **Via exemptionNo** — pass the certificate number directly in the request.

**Expected response:**
- `totalTax: 0` — the entire transaction is exempt

**Entity Use Codes reference:** https://developer.avalara.com/avatax/dev-guide/exemptions/exemptions-for-usage/

item.description:
## Purpose

Calculate sales tax in real time using the `CreateTransaction` API method. This is the core of the Avalara integration — every Fonteva checkout will call this endpoint.

## How it works

You send a `CreateTransactionModel` with:
- **companyCode** — identifies the TCH company in Avalara
- **customerCode** — unique customer identifier (mapped from Salesforce Account/Contact)
- **addresses** — `shipFrom` (TCH address) and `shipTo` (customer address) determine the tax jurisdiction
- **lines[]** — each Fonteva Sales Order Line becomes a line item with quantity, amount, and taxCode

Avalara returns the calculated tax per line and total, broken down by jurisdiction.

## Document Types

- **SalesOrder** — temporary estimate, not saved in Avalara. Use for cart/checkout preview.
- **SalesInvoice** — permanent record, saved in Avalara. Use after payment confirmation.

## Requests

- **3.1 SalesOrder (single line)** — basic tax estimate
- **3.2 SalesOrder (multiple lines)** — tests different tax codes (taxable, SaaS, non-taxable)
- **3.3 SalesOrder (exempt customer)** — tests `customerUsageType` exemption

## Doc
https://developer.avalara.com/products/avatax/api/methods/Transactions/CreateTransaction/

item.name: 4. Tax Lifecycle (Commit & Void)

exec: pm.test('Transaction created with Saved status', function () {

request.description:
## CreateTransaction — SalesInvoice (Permanent Record)

**API Method:** `CreateTransaction`
**Purpose:** Creates a permanent transaction record in Avalara. Unlike SalesOrder (folder 3), a SalesInvoice is saved and can be included in tax returns/filings.

**When TCH will use this:** After the customer confirms payment in Fonteva. The Apex `AvalaraTaxService.calculateTax()` method will call this with `type: SalesInvoice`.

**Key difference from SalesOrder:**
- `type: SalesInvoice` — permanent, gets a positive transaction ID
- `commit: false` — saved but not yet committed (allows for modifications before finalizing)

**Auto-sets variable:** `transactionCode` — used by requests 4.2 (CommitTransaction) and 4.3 (VoidTransaction)

**Expected response:**
- `status: Saved` — transaction is recorded but not yet committed
- `code` — unique transaction code
- `totalTax` — calculated tax amount

**Doc:** https://developer.avalara.com/products/avatax/api/methods/Transactions/CreateTransaction/

## CommitTransaction — Finalize for Tax Filing

**API Method:** `CommitTransaction`
**Purpose:** Changes the transaction status from `Saved` to `Committed`. A committed transaction is considered final and will be included in Avalara's Managed Returns (tax filing service).

**When TCH will use this:** After payment is fully processed in Fonteva. Can also be skipped if `commit: true` is set directly in the CreateTransaction request (auto-commit).

**Depends on:** Request 4.1 must be run first (auto-sets `transactionCode`).

**Request body:** `{ "commit": true }`

**Expected response:**
- `status: Committed`
- Same transaction data as before, with updated status

**Note:** Once committed, a transaction can only be voided or adjusted — it cannot be deleted.

**Doc:** https://developer.avalara.com/products/avatax/api/methods/Transactions/CommitTransaction/

## VoidTransaction — Cancel a Transaction

**API Method:** `VoidTransaction`
**Purpose:** Cancels a previously committed transaction. The transaction remains in Avalara's records but is excluded from tax filing. This is the equivalent of a full reversal.

**When TCH will use this:** When a Fonteva Sales Order is cancelled or a full refund is processed. The Apex `AvalaraTaxService.voidTransaction()` method will call this.

**Depends on:** Requests 4.1 and 4.2 must be run first.

**Request body:** `{ "code": "DocVoided" }` — the only supported void reason for full cancellation.

**Expected response:**
- `status: Cancelled`
- Transaction tax is effectively reversed

**Important:** For partial refunds, use `RefundTransaction` instead of `VoidTransaction`. Void is only for full cancellations.

**Doc:** https://developer.avalara.com/products/avatax/api/methods/Transactions/VoidTransaction/

item.description:
## Purpose

Tests the full transaction lifecycle in Avalara: **Create → Commit → Void**. This mirrors what happens in the Fonteva checkout flow when a payment is confirmed and later cancelled/refunded.

## Transaction States

```
SalesInvoice (commit: false) → status: Saved
         ↓ CommitTransaction
         → status: Committed (recorded for tax filing)
         ↓ VoidTransaction
         → status: Cancelled (removed from tax filing)
```

## When TCH will use each

- **CreateTransaction (SalesInvoice)** — after payment is confirmed in Fonteva. Creates a permanent record.
- **CommitTransaction** — marks the transaction as final. Can be done automatically by setting `commit: true` in CreateTransaction, or as a separate call.
- **VoidTransaction** — when a Fonteva order is cancelled or refunded. Removes the transaction from Avalara's tax filing.

## Important

Run these requests **in order** (4.1 → 4.2 → 4.3). Each step depends on the `transactionCode` auto-saved by the previous step.

## Docs
- CreateTransaction: https://developer.avalara.com/products/avatax/api/methods/Transactions/CreateTransaction/
- CommitTransaction: https://developer.avalara.com/products/avatax/api/methods/Transactions/CommitTransaction/
- VoidTransaction: https://developer.avalara.com/products/avatax/api/methods/Transactions/VoidTransaction/

item.name: 5. Exemption Certificate Management (ECM)

request.description:
## CreateCustomers — Register Customer in ECM

**API Method:** `CreateCustomers`
**Purpose:** Creates a customer record in Avalara's Exemption Certificate Management system. A customer must exist in ECM before certificates can be associated with them or CertExpress invitations can be sent.

**When TCH will use this:** The Apex `AvalaraExemptionService.createCustomer()` will call this when a customer needs to manage exemption certificates — triggered from the `avalaraCertExpressButton` LWC.

**Key fields:**
- `customerCode` — must match the `customerCode` used in `CreateTransaction` so Avalara can link certificates to transactions
- `name`, `line1`, `city`, `region`, `postalCode`, `country` — customer details
- `emailAddress` — used for CertExpress email invitations

**Note:** Uses numeric `companyId` in the URL (not the string `companyCode`). Run request 1.3 first.

**Doc:** https://developer.avalara.com/products/avatax/api/methods/Customers/CreateCustomers/

exec: console.log('No certificates found (expected for new test customer)');

request.description:
## ListCertificatesForCustomer — View Customer Certificates

**API Method:** `ListCertificatesForCustomer`
**Purpose:** Retrieves all exemption certificates associated with a customer. Returns certificate details including status (valid, expired, revoked), type, and expiration date.

**When TCH will use this:** The `avalaraCertificateViewer` LWC will call this to display a customer's certificates on the Account or Contact record page.

**Expected response:**
- `value[]` — array of certificate objects
- Each certificate includes: `id`, `status`, `signedDate`, `expirationDate`, `exposureZone`
- `@recordsetCount` — total number of certificates

**For a new test customer:** Expects 0 certificates (none uploaded yet).

**Doc:** https://developer.avalara.com/products/avatax/api/methods/Customers/ListCertificatesForCustomer/

## CreateCertExpressInvitation — Generate Upload Portal Link

**API Method:** `CreateCertExpressInvitation`
**Purpose:** Generates a CertExpress invitation — a unique URL to Avalara's hosted portal where the customer can upload their exemption certificate. Avalara handles the entire upload, validation, and storage process.

**When TCH will use this:** The `avalaraCertExpressButton` LWC calls this when a user clicks "Upload Tax Exemption Certificate". The returned URL is opened in a new tab, redirecting the customer to Avalara's CertExpress portal.

**Key fields:**
- `recipient` — email address for the invitation
- `coverLetterTitle` — template for the invitation email (`STANDARD_REQUEST`)
- `deliveryMethod` — `Email` (Avalara sends the invite) or `Download` (returns URL only)

**Expected response:**
- `requestLink` — the CertExpress portal URL to redirect the customer to
- `status` — invitation status

**Task requirement:** *"LWC button that will redirect to Avalara guest portal with user creation for tracking purposes"*

**Doc:** https://developer.avalara.com/products/avatax/api/methods/CertExpressInvites/CreateCertExpressInvitation/

## DownloadCertificateImage — Download Certificate Document

**API Method:** `DownloadCertificateImage`
**Purpose:** Downloads the image or PDF of an exemption certificate that was uploaded by the customer via CertExpress.

**When TCH will use this:** Backoffice LWC to preview/review certificates submitted by customers. Enables admin review without needing ECM subscription UI access.

**Prerequisites:**
- A certificate must exist (customer uploaded via CertExpress link)
- Set `certificateId` variable from the response of 5.2 ListCertificatesForCustomer

**Query parameter:** `$type` — `pdf` or `jpeg`

**Expected response:** Binary file (PDF or JPEG image of the certificate)

**Discovery (2026-05-15):** This API works without ECM subscription, even though the Avalara admin UI blocks image preview.

**Doc:** https://developer.avalara.com/api-reference/avatax/rest/v2/methods/Certificates/DownloadCertificateImage/

## GetCertificate — Get Single Certificate Details

**API Method:** `GetCertificate`
**Purpose:** Retrieves full details of a specific certificate by ID. Returns metadata including status, signed date, expiration date, exposure zone, exempt reason, and linked customers.

**When TCH will use this:** Backoffice detail view — when an admin clicks on a specific certificate from the list to see full details.

**Prerequisites:** Set `certificateId` from the response of 5.2 ListCertificatesForCustomer.

**Expected response:** Single certificate object with all fields.

**Doc:** https://developer.avalara.com/api-reference/avatax/rest/v2/methods/Certificates/GetCertificate/

exec: console.log('ID: ' + cert.id + ' | Status: ' + cert.status + ' | Created: ' + cert.createdDate);

request.description:
## QueryCertificates — Search/Filter All Certificates

**API Method:** `QueryCertificates`
**Purpose:** Queries all certificates for the company with filtering, sorting, and pagination. Useful for backoffice dashboards and reporting.

**When TCH will use this:** Admin dashboard showing all certificates across all customers, with ability to filter by status, region, or date.

**Useful query parameters:**
- `$filter` — e.g., `status eq 'COMPLETE'` or `exposureZone/name eq 'Alabama'`
- `$top` — page size
- `$skip` — offset for pagination
- `$orderBy` — e.g., `createdDate DESC`

**Expected response:** Paginated list of certificate objects with `@recordsetCount`.

**Doc:** https://developer.avalara.com/api-reference/avatax/rest/v2/methods/Certificates/QueryCertificates/

exec: console.log('No valid certificates found for this customer/region');

request.description:
## ListValidCertificatesForCustomer — Check Valid Exemptions

**API Method:** `ListValidCertificatesForCustomer`
**Purpose:** Returns only VALID (non-expired, non-revoked) certificates for a customer, filtered by country and region. This is the key API for determining if a customer is currently exempt in a specific jurisdiction.

**When TCH will use this:** During checkout — before calling CreateTransaction, check if the customer has a valid exemption for the shipping state. Can also be used to show exemption status badges in the UI.

**Query parameters:**
- `country` — e.g., `US`
- `region` — state code, e.g., `AL` (Alabama)

**Expected response:**
- If valid certificate exists: array with certificate details
- If no valid certificate: empty array

**Note:** Change `region` parameter to match the state where you created a test certificate.

**Doc:** https://developer.avalara.com/api-reference/avatax/rest/v2/methods/Customers/ListValidCertificatesForCustomer/

## UpdateCertificate — Update Certificate Metadata

**API Method:** `UpdateCertificate`
**Purpose:** Updates an existing certificate's metadata. Can be used to change status (e.g., revoke), update expiration date, or modify other fields.

**When TCH will use this:** Backoffice action — admin revokes or updates a certificate. For example, marking a certificate as REVOKED when a customer loses their exempt status.

**Common use cases:**
- Revoke: set `status` to `REVOKED`
- Update expiration: change `expirationDate`

**Prerequisites:** Set `certificateId`. Adjust the body fields as needed — the example revokes the certificate.

**Caution:** This is a PUT (full replace). You may need to include all required fields from GetCertificate response, not just the changed field. Test to confirm behavior.

**Doc:** https://developer.avalara.com/api-reference/avatax/rest/v2/methods/Certificates/UpdateCertificate/

## UnlinkCertificatesFromCustomer — Remove Certificate from Customer

**API Method:** `UnlinkCertificatesFromCustomer`
**Purpose:** Removes the association between a certificate and a customer WITHOUT deleting the certificate. The certificate still exists in the system but no longer applies to this customer's transactions.

**When TCH will use this:** Backoffice action — when a customer should no longer be exempt but the certificate itself should be preserved (e.g., for audit trail). Safer alternative to DeleteCertificate.

**Why prefer Unlink over Delete:**
- Unlink: removes from ONE customer, certificate preserved for other linked customers and audit
- Delete: permanently removes from ALL linked customers

**Prerequisites:** Set `certificateId` and `customerCode`.

**Expected response:** Updated customer-certificate relationship.

**Doc:** https://developer.avalara.com/api-reference/avatax/rest/v2/methods/Certificates/UnlinkCertificatesFromCustomer/

item.description:
## Purpose

Manage tax exemption certificates for TCH customers. Some customers (government agencies, non-profits, resellers) are exempt from sales tax and must provide exemption certificates as proof.

## How ECM integrates with tax calculation

When a customer has a valid certificate stored in Avalara's ECM, the `CreateTransaction` API automatically applies the exemption — no extra logic needed. Just send the correct `customerCode`.

## The CertExpress flow (from the task requirements)

The task specifies:

> "LWC button that will redirect to Avalara guest portal with user creation for tracking purposes" 
  

This is the **CertExpress** flow:

1. **CreateCustomers** (5.1) — register the customer in ECM
    
2. **CreateCertExpressInvitation** (5.3) — generate a portal invite URL
    
3. Customer clicks the URL → uploads their certificate on Avalara's hosted portal
    
4. **ListCertificatesForCustomer** (5.2) — query certificates to display in the LWC viewer
    

## Backoffice review flow

1. **DownloadCertificateImage** (5.4) — download the uploaded certificate PDF/image
    
2. **GetCertificate** (5.5) — get full certificate details
    
3. **QueryCertificates** (5.6) — search/filter all certificates (dashboard)
    
4. **ListValidCertificatesForCustomer** (5.7) — check valid exemptions for a state (checkout)
    
5. **UpdateCertificate** (5.8) — update metadata or revoke
    
6. **UnlinkCertificatesFromCustomer** (5.9) — remove certificate from customer (safe delete)
    

## Prerequisites

- Run request 1.3 (GetCompanies) first to populate the `companyId` variable
    
- Run 5.2 after a certificate exists to auto-set `certificateId` for requests 5.4-5.9
    
- ECM endpoints use the numeric `companyId`, not the string `companyCode`
    

## Doc

[https://developer.avalara.com/products/ecm/api/certcapture/](https://developer.avalara.com/products/ecm/api/certcapture/)

item.name: 6. Definitions & Lookup

request.description:
## ListEntityUseCodes — Exemption Reason Codes

**API Method:** `ListEntityUseCodes`
**Purpose:** Returns the full list of Entity Use Codes — standardized reason codes that classify why a customer is exempt from tax. These codes are used in the `customerUsageType` field of `CreateTransaction`.

**Common codes:**
- `A` — Federal Government
- `B` — State Government
- `C` — Tribal Government
- `D` — Foreign Diplomat
- `E` — Charitable/Religious Organization
- `F` — Religious Organization
- `G` — Resale
- `H` — Agricultural Production
- `L` — Other/Custom

**When TCH will use this:** To populate a dropdown in the UI where admins assign an exemption type to a customer account. The selected code is stored on the Account record and sent with every `CreateTransaction` request for that customer.

**Doc:** https://developer.avalara.com/products/avatax/api/methods/Definitions/ListEntityUseCodes/

## ListTaxCodes — Product Tax Categories

**API Method:** `ListTaxCodes`
**Purpose:** Returns Avalara's catalog of Tax Codes — categories that define how a product is taxed across different jurisdictions. Each Fonteva Item must be mapped to the correct Tax Code.

**Common codes for TCH:**
- `P0000000` — Tangible Personal Property (default taxable goods)
- `SW054000` — SaaS / Cloud-based Software
- `SP0000000` — Services
- `NT` — Non-Taxable
- `D9999999` — Digital Goods

**Why this matters:** A membership fee, a software subscription, and a physical product are all taxed differently depending on the state. Assigning the wrong tax code means calculating the wrong tax rate.

**Recommendation:** Add a `Tax_Code__c` custom field to the Fonteva `OrderApi__Item__c` object so business users can manage the mapping without code changes.

**Doc:** https://developer.avalara.com/products/avatax/api/methods/Definitions/ListTaxCodes/

exec: if (count === 0) console.log('WARNING: No nexus configured. Tax calculations will return $0.');

request.description:
## ListNexusByCompany — Tax Obligation by State

**API Method:** `ListNexusByCompany`
**Purpose:** Lists all nexus declarations for the company — the states and jurisdictions where TCH is legally obligated to collect and remit sales tax.

**What is nexus?** A legal connection between a company and a state that creates a tax collection obligation. Created by having a physical presence (office, employees, warehouse) or exceeding a sales volume threshold in that state.

**Why this is critical for testing:** If no nexus is configured for a state, `CreateTransaction` will return **$0 tax** for customers in that state — even if the product is normally taxable. This is the #1 cause of unexpected $0 results during development.

**Expected response:**
- List of nexus declarations with `region` (state), `country`, `jurisName` (jurisdiction name)
- If empty: **WARNING** — tax calculations will return $0 for all states. Nexus must be configured in the Avalara admin portal.

**Note:** Uses numeric `companyId` in the URL. Run request 1.3 first.

**Doc:** https://developer.avalara.com/products/avatax/api/methods/Nexus/ListNexusByCompany/

item.description:
## Purpose

Reference data endpoints that return Avalara's configuration and lookup tables. These are read-only APIs used for:
- Populating UI dropdowns (entity use codes, tax codes)
- Verifying portal configuration (nexus declarations)
- Mapping Fonteva products to Avalara tax categories

## Requests

- **6.1 ListEntityUseCodes** — exemption reason codes (Federal Gov, State Gov, Religious, etc.)
- **6.2 ListTaxCodes** — product tax categories (tangible goods, SaaS, services, non-taxable)
- **6.3 ListNexusByCompany** — which states TCH is configured to collect tax in

## Why 6.3 (Nexus) is important

If no nexus is configured for a state, `CreateTransaction` will return $0 tax for that state — even if the product is normally taxable. This is the most common reason for unexpected $0 results during testing.
